Put one line in the register for each person the gate must judge

scope_expand.Rd

The gate asks of a requester "could you have done this by hand". What the channel executes can have been written by more than one person, and the rule is the same for all of them: whoever wrote what is executed must be able to do it by hand. The rights of whoever approves are not checked, because approving is not writing: it adds no power to the change.

Usage

scope_expand(register, subjects)

Arguments

register

The register as a data frame, carrying at least record_id, server and project_id.

subjects

A list as long as the rows of register, each element the usernames to judge for that row.

Value

register with one line per row and subject, in the order of the rows and then of the subjects, and requested_by equal to the subject.

Details

This turns a register and the people to judge for each of its rows into a register scope_errors() can read: one line per row and subject, with requested_by set to the subject. A row with nobody to judge stays once, with an empty requested_by, so that scope_errors() refuses it as not attributed and it does not slip through for lack of a name.
